content: Rifabutin, commonly sold under the brand name Mycobutin, is a rifamycin antibiotic used to prevent and treat bacterial infections, particularly Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC). It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. This medication can be used alone or in combination with other drugs, depending on the condition being treated. How to Use: Rifabutin is taken orally, either with or without food, as directed by your doctor, typically once or twice daily. If stomach upset occurs, it is recommended to take it with food. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, weight, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. To achieve the best results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and continue the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve before completion. Side Effects: Common side effects include diarrhea, stomach upset, changes in taste, nausea, or vomiting. Rifabutin may also cause harmless discoloration of bodily fluids, such as urine, sweat, saliva, or tears, turning them a brown-orange color. This effect will resolve once the medication is discontinued. Rarely, this drug may cause a severe intestinal condition due to Clostridium difficile (C. diff) bacteria, which can occur during or even weeks to months after treatment. Serious allergic reactions are rare but possible. Other potential side effects include: Discoloration of urine (30%) Neutropenia (25%) Leukopenia (17%) Rash (11%) Elevated liver enzymes (AST/ALT) (7-9%) Thrombocytopenia (5%) Abdominal pain, diarrhea, eructation (belching), headache, nausea/vomiting, anorexia, and flatulence (2-4%) Anemia, myalgia, and other blood/lymphatic disorders (e.g., agranulocytosis, lymphopenia, granulocytopenia, decreased white blood cell or neutrophil counts, and reduced platelet counts) Immune system disorders such as hypersensitivity reactions, bronchospasm, and shock Gastrointestinal issues like C. difficile-associated colitis Severe skin reactions, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS), toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), and acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP) Joint stiffness, swelling, tenderness, or paresthesia, which may indicate arthralgias or myositis Brown-orange discoloration of bodily fluids, including urine, feces, saliva, sputum, sweat, tears, and skin Precautions: Before taking rifabutin, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, other rifamycins (e.g., rifampin), or any other substances. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Rifabutin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, rifabutin should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk, but women with HIV should not breastfeed due to the risk of transmitting the virus. Drug Interactions: Rifabutin can interact with other medications, potentially altering their effectiveness or increasing the risk of side effects. It accelerates the removal of certain drugs from the body, which may reduce their efficacy. For example, rifabutin may decrease the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods (e.g., pills, patches, or rings), increasing the risk of pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor whether you should use additional reliable birth control methods while taking this medication. Monitoring: Regular medical and laboratory tests, such as liver function tests and complete blood counts, are recommended while taking rifabutin. Physicians should monitor for potential side effects like neutropenia or thrombocytopenia, especially during long-term use. Patients co-administered rifabutin with clarithromycin or fluconazole should be closely monitored for uveitis, a potential side effect. If uveitis is suspected, consult an ophthalmologist and consider discontinuing therapy. Storage: Store rifabutin at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed by your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into drains unless directed to do so. Overdose: In the event of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention. In the U.S., call 911 for severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing. Alternatively, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. Important Notes: This summary does not include all possible information about rifabutin. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete details about this medication and your specific health needs.
